Data Vortex A'26 — Round 3: Real-Time Social Monitoring¶

WhatsApp Privacy Policy 2021: Backlash, Sentiment Shifts & Migration Analysis¶

Team: Event Horizon
Topic: WhatsApp privacy policy backlash, public sentiment shifts, and migration to Signal/Telegram

Analytical Timeline¶

Phase Period Description
T-0 (Baseline) Nov 1 – Dec 31, 2020 Normal discourse, stable sentiment
T+1 (Shock) Jan 1 – Jan 31, 2021 Policy announced, viral backlash
T+2 (Fallout) Feb 1 – Jul 31, 2021 Migration wave, regulatory responses

Data Summary¶

  • Primary dataset: WhatsApp + Telegram Play Store reviews (Kaggle, filtered to topic window)
  • Bonus live-scraped: GDELT global news headlines + Hacker News discussions (API-collected)
  • Total rows: 14,891 | Sources: 4 distinct | Date coverage: Nov 2020 – Jul 2021

Narrative flow: Load & inspect → Sentiment analysis → ATSA → LDA topic evolution → Activity spikes → Entity extraction → Interpretation

2. Aspect-Term Sentiment Analysis (ATSA)¶

For each key topic term (privacy, telegram, signal, facebook, etc.), we extract all posts containing that term and compute: average sentiment, negative ratio, and a WhatsApp-vs-Telegram sentiment comparison. This confirms term-level sentiment around the migration narrative.

Key expectation: Posts mentioning telegram or signal should show higher positive sentiment than posts mentioning privacy or terms (which carry the backlash signal).

6. Named Entity Analysis — Top Extracted Terms¶

spaCy NER (en_core_web_sm) run across all 14,891 posts. Entity types captured: ORG, PRODUCT, GPE, PERSON, LAW, NORP, EVENT. HTML artifacts cleaned post-extraction.

Critical finding: Signal (4,871) and Telegram (4,036) rank 2nd and 3rd globally, confirming that the backlash discourse was inseparable from migration intent.

Top entities: [('whatsapp', 5525), ('signal', 4871), ('telegram', 4036), ('google', 385), ('apple', 373)]

7. Interpretation: Baseline → Shock → Migration¶

Confirmed Narrative Arc¶

T-0 (Baseline, Nov-Dec 2020):
648 posts, stable sentiment (~0.35 average). Normal app review discourse. No policy-related spikes. GDELT headlines minimal on WhatsApp privacy. LDA topics: general app features, early EU GDPR mentions.

T+1 (Shock, Jan 2021):
5,941 posts — a 917% volume increase from baseline. Peak spike: 743 posts on Jan 7 (z=2.19).
Sentiment drops sharply (avg -0.15 on Jan 7 vs +0.35 baseline). 20 sentiment shifts detected.
Trigger: Jan 4 in-app ToS notice + Jan 7 Elon Musk tweet ('Use Signal') went viral globally.
LDA topics shift to signal/telegram/switch/privacy — unmistakable migration framing.

T+2 (Fallout, Feb-Jul 2021):
4,373 posts. Sustained elevated volume (above baseline) throughout.
Secondary spikes: Apr 7 (CCI probe, z=2.23), May 8 (deadline extension, z=2.25).
Sentiment gradually normalizes (mean returns to ~0.25) as the acute crisis passes.
Entity analysis: India (282 mentions) reflects the outsized regulatory and user reaction in the subcontinent.
